a.text: ...As much as we value the young, youth is never an excuse for crime and depravity.
In Ursus, children younger than them are already contributing to the empire in their respective ways; in the armies, in the factories, in the mines.
It is only the rich, spoiled students who cry foul at those who tell them to rein in their babbling mouths, as though Ursus would fall if they stopped talking for a moment.

They have never seen battle nor borne the weight of their comrades on their shoulders, yet they read their newspapers and play with their sandboxes and maps, dreaming of encirclements and flanking maneuvers, of 'victory at any cost'.

They have never spent a moment working the factories, or watching the desperate workers when a production line is halted in the middle of the night, yet they fool themselves with slogans like 'double the pay, double the production'.
They flock into the birch forests, writing sorry poems that would have you believe their lives were more pathetic than the miners of the Far North.

Their views are based on their shallow understanding of the land around them. They appropriate the words of their forebears to support their fallacies, repeating themselves over and over to convince those foolish enough to hold such views.
The only mistake of this council is its continued indulgence and restraint. It has gained nothing but their scorn and hatred, and birthed these outcomes.
I maintain that this hearing is completely redundant, because the nature of the incident at issue is clear.
The students are attempting to undermine Ursine order. They have taken up arms and broken down the walls of the containment zone. This is no less than premediated insurrection.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: As for their 'leader', this so-called 'The General'—

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: —This Sonya Mikhailivna.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: She is a traitor to Ursus, plain and simple.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Your opinion is respected, Count Yusupov, but we cannot make a determination as to these students until the hearing is concluded.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: I will once again remind all present that the outcome of this hearing will define the Katorga Incident.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: This atrocity that took place in our magnificent Grypherburg must be judged fairly and solemnly.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: And we must ensure a fair outcome for the future of Ursus, these students living in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: Your Honor, I must remind you before we begin...

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: The actions of these students that currently stand outside the council building have tarnished the dignity of Ursus.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: The emblem of our empire hangs above your head. It reminds us all from whence the glory of Ursus arises, the glory in which all her people bathe.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: As the Grypherburg of old belongs likewise to the emperors of old, the present and future belong to His Reigning Majesty, and to all of us who execute Ursus's will on his behalf.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: If we fail to try Sonya Mykhailivna and her accomplices for treason, we are handing the future over to the lazy, unproductive dregs of society.

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: How, then, could Ursus hold her head high upon this land? How could His Imperial Majesty's justice be upheld?

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: Justice? How dare you speak of His Majesty's justice?

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: No lawyers, no prosecutors, no juries... the motion to establish a statute has been on the agenda for more than a decade. The old guard like you are the only reason it hasn't been passed!

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: And what have the new blood like you done for the empire? You've bought your titles with chervontsy, yet you consort with traitors...

steps.name: Scathing Noble
steps.text: How dare you adorn your chest with the medals conferred upon you by His Imperial Majesty, when you step up from those protesting students outside to wax lyrical here. Have you no shame?
Meanwhile, outside the council building.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Damned kids...
He was supposed to be off-duty today.
That is, until he got an urgent call while sleeping in his room, and was told that students from all over Grypherburg are on the streets, blocking every route to the council building.
He and his colleagues mobilized for war, yet when they came on the scene...
They found no flags, no shouting, only students standing on the streets quietly.
They give way when police or officials show up, allowing them to enter the 'siege'.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Stop right there! What are you doing?

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: Remain calm, sir. We mean no disrespect. We're only here to support our fellow students.

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: But some dignitaries have promised to speak at the hearing, and now they are nowhere to be seen.

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: May I ask if the police have them in custody? We can't allow the hearing to begin without them—

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: I don't know what you're talking about! This is none of your business!

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Now, get back!

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: Where are our people? Why are there so many absences?

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: Have the old fools detained our witnesses to give themselves an advantage?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Order!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: The police have been mobilized to maintain order in Grypherburg, given the circumstances. Traffic disruption may cause delays.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: However, this matter can permit no further delay. While you were arguing, our first witnessed arrived.
The bickering belligerents turn to the door, their anger replaced with curiosity as they watch the Ursus woman enter the hall.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Please take your seats. Let the proceedings commence, in the name of His Imperial Majesty's justice...

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Witness, proceed to the stand.

steps.name: Whispering Noble A
steps.text: This is a friend of Sonya Mykhailivna?

steps.name: Whispering Noble B
steps.text: Yes. They say the new nobility vouched for her. As long as she plays her part and testifies as agreed, her friend will get off easy.

steps.name: Whispering Noble A
steps.text: But that's not the outcome we want to see...

steps.name: Whispering Noble B
steps.text: Relax. I want to see how much weight these commoners' words carry.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Thank you for testifying, Young Zoya.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: I'm sure you have noticed the police equipment that Zoya carries.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Her father was a respected Ursine policeman, who gave his life at Chernobog to protect the empire's order. I am sure she carries on her father's loyalty to the land.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: As an eyewitness to the Katorga Incident, she was questioned several days ago, and submitted a report regarding the matter.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: The committee will now read the report and cross-examine the witness. I believe this report will give all of us a better understanding of the Katorga Incident.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Young Zoya, do you attest to the truthfulness of this document, and to the statements that you will give at this hearing?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I do, Your Honor.

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: Your Honor, we request the hearing be postponed.

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: Young Zoya's guarantor, Baron Kamshalov, has not yet arrived. The baron's honor is at stake when she testifies. She must not be allowed to do so in his absence.

steps.name: Unconcerned Noble
steps.text: Hah, everyone knows Baron Kamshalov likes to sleep in. Are we to postpone the hearing permanently, when he never wakes up?

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: I am unaware that he has any such habit.

steps.name: Unconcerned Noble
steps.text: You think his casinos operate in the daylight? He does his business late at night.

steps.name: Unconcerned Noble
steps.text: You may both be barons now, but he had already made more money than you will in two lifetimes by the time you were just a private in the army.

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: But he wasn't there last night—

Someone beside him grabs him, and he stops himself mid-sentence, sweating profusely from his forehead. He can hardly admit in public that he and other friends in high places spent last night in an illegal casino.

steps.name: Unconcerned Noble
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Unconcerned Noble
steps.text: If he wasn't at the casino last night, maybe you should ask your wife—

steps.name: Noble Beneath Podium
steps.text: Say that again, mudak!
The furious noble jumps across a few rows of seats to get at the other.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Police! Separate them!
The arbiter's shouting ignites a council hall that was already on the brink of inferno, with several who were already arguing joining the fray.
The few policemen in the room walk up and motion to try to separate them, but stop short of touching anyone. All the belligerents are too important for them to risk angering.

Absinthe closes her eyes and touches the back of her neck. For a moment there, she thinks it might be the air stirred by the swinging of fists that is making her feel cold, not the behavior of the nobles once again going beyond the pale.
In her mind, she seems to hear the words that every person in Ursus has heard a thousand times.

a.text: You're the reason Ursus is what it is!

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: ...You're the reason Ursus is what it is!

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: So much the better! Do we dare to imagine the empire if you were guiding her?
They grab each other by the collar, while the onlooking students seem to have no intention of stopping then, instead cheering them on in eager anticipation of a good show.
Several students sit quietly in the rear, away from the crowd.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Is Sonya not here yet?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Reviewing the correspondence, Sonya should be here this afternoon, and Instructor Dur-nar tomorrow.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: But the discussion has meandered onto a tangent. Should we intervene before things get out of hand?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: We're participating in a student gathering under the banner of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group, with Sonya as our leader. I doubt anyone will listen to us without her present.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Besides, the issues being discussed here are important. We need her to make decisions.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: But I recall that Sonya did not part on the best of terms with Olga's group—

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: That's the last honey drop, Leto!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You're the kindest and sweetest, Gummy. Maybe there's another hidden somewhere in your pocket?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Don't pick on Gummy over a piece of candy, Leto.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's because you wouldn't let me drink honey... I haven't had a sip since I got back to Ursus.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I should've stayed in Kjerag.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: We're not here on vacation... you can have all the honey you want once we complete our mission from the Grypherburg office, or when you stop getting honey drunk.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Boooooring...

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: You sure you don't want to watch them fight, Leto? I thought you of all people would be excited.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I like fighting, but I don't care about two dunces slugging it out. They talk about helping people, but the first thing they do is punch the people who are supposed to help them.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hm? Looks like the one in charge has finally had enough.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: People... people! That's enough!
The golden-haired Ursus screams at the top of her lungs, but her anxious, trembling voice sounds thin and weak amidst the cheers and angry shouts.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: People... let's set these pointless arguments aside. Don't forget why we're here today.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Rania is a Grypherburg student. He's one of us, our friend, and he has been treated unjustly because of an act of justice.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I am only so strong alone, but there must be something that the combined strength of the Student Assembly can do, to make the capital hear our voices.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Let's calm down, and work out a plan to free our friend from prison.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: No point in discussing the big picture with a bunch of meat heads.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: Rania's actions were reckless. Did he not think through the consequences when he vandalized the council hall?

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: You hear them, Olga? The Symposium doesn't want to help Rania. They are defeatists who keep using the 'big picture' as an excuse to shirk their responsibilities.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: Rania is your friend and a member of the Petrachevsky Group, but the Vanguards have always been on your side.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: Meanwhile, this coward's grandfather might have been an honorary captain in the old Emperor's Imperial Guard, but he has none of the spirit of an Ursus soldier!

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: The Symposium is of one mind with you, Olga. We have never opposed rescuing Rania and the other detained students, and we do not even oppose the use of force when necessary.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: Meanwhile, what do these Vanguards think their crude, barbaric actions would actually serve to achieve when it comes to changing our country?

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: The Revitalization of Ursus makes it clear that the empire is not an old jacket you can simply swap out for a new one.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: That damnable Nikola Ilyinsky again...

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I would be happy to hear the Symposium out, if you have any better ideas.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: We must print more newspapers, highlighting the injustices Rania and his comrades have suffered.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: Not just in the academies; we have to mobilize the citizenry as well. Rania was arrested for speaking up for the miners of the Far North. The workers will stand on our side.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: We will attract sympathizers by publicizing the plight of the arrested students, we will teach them why we struggle, and how to struggle. We will target the legacy of Hippogryphs.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: The old nobles of Ursus gladly accepted the brutal traditions of the Hippogryph Kingdom. Many of them have Hippogryph blood in their veins.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: Only by excising these centuries-old tumors can Ursus truly belong to the Ursus.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: What a joke. Do these 'old nobles' include the House of Treplev? Are you going to excise Olga like a tumor?

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: That is another matter entirely. As long as they support a new Ursus—

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: Then you tell the burghers and workers that Nikola Ilyinsky never proposed overthrowing the regime, only how to sell himself for a good price afterwards.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: And then you tell the Liberi and Felines among them that Ursus belongs to the Ursus, and all other races are either our servants or spies.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: You're taking things out of context! He never said anything of the sort.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: The only thing the old tsar did right was hang this madman who kept babbling about a 'new Ursine identity'!
A student beneath the podium throws a metal water can at the Vanguards member, but it misses and hits the stage instead.
Other Vanguards immediately grab him and start beating him up, once again engulfing the scene in chaos.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, these guys don't call themselves Vanguards for nothing. They fight a little better, relatively speaking.
The ruckus is making it impossible for Absinthe to respond to Leto's joke. She glances at Olga, who is supposed to be in charge.
Olga stands quietly with hesitation on her face, looking at the members of the Self-Government Group, the only ones who have not involved themselves in the clash.

steps.name: Vanguards Member
steps.text: ...We have new problems.
Punches freeze in mid-air and the shouting ceases. The brawling students let go of each other.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: General!

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You're late again, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: But it looks like I'm here just in time.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: You were late for the last general meeting. Need I remind you that a general meeting of the Student Assembly represents—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: A major event that will determine the future of Grypherburg's students. I remember. Go on, keep 'talking'.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why so quiet, Faddey? I thought you liked greeting people with your fists, including me.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Not like that'd achieve anything.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No, but talking with your fists always guarantees a result better than talking with your mouth.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: It's true that today's agenda has not advanced smoothly. But that doesn't excuse the Self-Government Group's repeated contempt for the Student Assembly.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Excuse me, Chairman Trepleva, but what exactly do you mean by 'contempt'?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: The Self-Government Group has followed the Assembly's rules to the letter and participated in all activities since we joined.
Everyone turns to look at Zima.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: This general meeting is being held on short notice, while many of the Self-Government Group's members have missions abroad. I find it unfair that you are accusing us of contempt simply for being late.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Most importantly, the Self-Government Group has never been party to the Assembly's internal conflicts.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: If I may be blunt, it seems the Self-Government Group has respected the Assembly to a greater extent than any of the student organizations arguing and fighting in this room.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: If I may be blunt, Anna, you were never supposed to be part of the Assembly.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: Your organization and its members are from Chernobog, while we are all Grypherburgers.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I remind you that it was Olga who extended an invitation to the Self-Government Group to join the Assembly.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: Olga wanted the Assembly to unite as many students as possible. That's why she took you in, and provided assistance for you to establish a base in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Symposium Member
steps.text: In turn, you are expected to demonstrate an eagerness to contribute to the Assembly, or at the very least, to respect it.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: We have not forgotten the help that we received, and we express our gratitude for it, Leonid.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: The Self-Government Group has always been supportive of the Assembly's activities. We have never backed down, nor compromised your plans.

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: What did you do when the assembly instructed you to burn the tsar's portrait?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: We upgraded the portrait to a scrawling of the tsar's family. Something wrong with that?

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: Whose scrawling was it?

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Mine, hehe.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: It was my first time. Everyone loved it!

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: That's the problem!

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: How do you expect to provoke anti-tsarist sentiment when you draw the tsar's family so cute?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: So the problem is she draws too good? You couldn't catch her if you practiced three years!

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Suka! You're just looking for trouble!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: That's enough! Stop—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: ...Order! This is a hearing, a solemn occasion. We will tolerate no disruptions.
Absinthe wakes from her reverie. The nobles have reached a truce, though they continue to glare at each other, their fine outfits not looking so fine anymore.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Very well. Let us return to your background, Young Zoya.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: You mentioned the Student Assembly, an organization that I'm sure most of us are familiar with.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: It is an alliance of student organizations from various schools, often publishing commentary under pseudonyms inspired by famous traitors, such as the wicked Ivan Tulin

steps.name: Whispering Noble A
steps.text: Hey... who is this Ivan Tulin

steps.name: Whispering Noble B
steps.text: Younger brother of the great traitor Yakov Petrov, who wrote several seditious volumes while in exile in Leithanien.

steps.name: Whispering Noble B
steps.text: The council has investigated, but he hasn't been seen in public for a while, and he hasn't published anything new in some time, so he's probably dead.

steps.name: Whispering Noble A
steps.text: Why use the name of a dead man?

steps.name: Whispering Noble B
steps.text: All these conspiracies and outlandish claims need a representative opposed to His Imperial Majesty, preferably someone who cannot personally rebuke them.

steps.name: Whispering Noble B
steps.text: They all want Ivan dead more than we do, so that they might claim the name.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: You said you personally witnessed the meeting of this Student Assembly as a spectator before the incident?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I should make it clear that I was not a member of any student organization; I attended as a friend of Sonya's, and others.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I do not have full knowledge of the outcome of their discussions, and I never supported their actions.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Parliamentarian, pass me the document to your left.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: This transcript indicates that the Student Assembly was planning some kind of action against the Grypherburg Winter Ball.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: That's enough... we've wasted too much time already. We must get back to the agenda at hand—how to rescue Rania and his comrades.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Faddey, you are the Vanguards' representative. What is your final proposal?

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: We’ve deliberated fully. A raid on the prison.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: While Rania's arrest was a high-profile one, we have learned that his prison is not heavily guarded.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Besides, the annual ball presents a waning of Grypherburg's security. It's the perfect opportunity.

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: You're out of your mind!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: (Whisper) Wouldn't the police be extra careful with all the nobles gathered during the ball?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: (Whisper) Father said the Grypherburg police are not selected by the law, but appointed by the powerful.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: (Whisper) Both the armies and the police are part of the Ursus Guard. Minor nobles who don't have the influence to send their children into the Army as officers take the second-best option of sending them into the police to 'gain experience'.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: (Whisper) The Winter Ball is more than just a social event; it's also the stage of politics and intrigue for all the assembled nobility.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: (Whisper) Personnel moves in the police normally take place before and after the ball, which will keep the officials busy.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: (Whisper) And so, Faddey is not necessarily wrong.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: You're proposing an act of war, Faddey, while I'm not sure you can even wield a weapon, nor have I seen any preparation from your party.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Of course we're prepared.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: This is for present company only, but I will tell you that I know some free traders who can get us used weapons from the Londinium war, enough to arm us all.

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: Free traders? Those foreigners?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Is that enough to face down heavily-armed prison guards?

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Of course! If you've seen them with your own eyes, you know that they're decades ahead of Ursine technology.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: We're falling behind. Survival of the fittest is the law of nature. This is our last chance to catch up.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: We must not allow the old, corrupt aristocrats to drag the empire into its grave. We will be the vanguard that makes Ursus strong again.

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: And you think these 'free traders' do it out of the goodness of their hearts? Have you forgotten that we are Ursines first and foremost?

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: You would have us take up foreign weapons and follow the corrupt institutions of Victoria and Columbia! I will not stand idly by while people like you—
He steps forward as he shouts, trying to prove the Symposium are just as physically capable.
Someone grabs his right arm. He tries to shake off the hand, only to find that it does not budge in the slightest.
Leonid turns around to curse the interloper, only for his gaze to meet Zima's.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Are you done?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Faddey, your plan is just sending people to die. No intel, no tactics, no info on whether the weapons are any good.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The police will be a little mixed up, but the prison is defended by trained gendarmes that we can't handle.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: I know you can fight, Sonya. Many of us Vanguards have great respect for you.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: But your talk of 'ready' is no different from the Symposium's 'big picture', both excuses for inaction.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Do not interfere with the Assembly's decision, if you don't have a better way to get Rania and his comrades out.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Do not presume to represent the Assembly's decision without a general vote, Faddey.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: The Symposium is clearly not on your side, and the Self-Government Group will not support a suicide mission. We can take a vote now, if you really think your words are enough to sway the majority.
All eyes are on Olga, filled with hope and expectation.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Olga, if there are no objections, the Petrachevsky Group can count the votes as usual—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Olga?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I agree with Leonid and Sonya. The Assembly cannot risk a failed violent struggle.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: But I also agree that simply sitting around will only make matters worse, sapping our will to resist while giving the police the chance to do as they please with Rania.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Therefore, I have a plan that will satisfy everyone and rescue Rania. We will encircle the Winter Ball.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What is she talking about? Instead of raiding the prison, we go straight for the nobles?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: No, this is not an act of violence.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: We will go unarmed. We will protest with signs in our hands and tell the nobles about the people who are undermining our nation's future behind our backs.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I don't see the point in it.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Your father may be a good man, Olga, but that doesn't mean all the nobility are willing to sit and talk with us.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Even setting aside everything they've done over the years, they have arrested Rania and his comrades, and they're talking about making a public example of them.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You would simply yell at them, empty-handed and defenseless...? This is like putting a plate of fresh meat out for a mangler, cut to bite-sized pieces for the beast's convenience.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: No, Anna, you don't understand. The nobles at the ball have no reason to harm us.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I've organized similar events in the past. As long as we exercise restraint, neither the nobles nor the police will lay hands on us.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: In the name of my father, I promise that this is simply an action to make our voices heard. No one will get hurt.

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: I agree with Olga. Many of our number come from the local aristocracy. In effect, we will be holding ourselves hostage against the aristocratic class as a whole.

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: It's one of the few chips that we truly hold in our own hands. With enough of us, it's very possible that we can sway the council's decision.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: A compromise, but better than inaction... the Vanguards assent.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Let us take the vote.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: It is hereby proposed that all the constituent organizations of Student Assembly march upon the venue and protest before the nobility at seven o'clock in the evening, three days from now, during the Winter Ball.
Hands raise into the air... before long, there are a few outsiders at the meeting, just as there were during the brawl.
The students with their hands raised look so tall, their calm giving them strength.
Absinthe is short of breath. She scans their faces, but finds no reassurance in them.
Some desire action, their eyes filled with anger, their hands trembling with guilt towards their fellow students and hatred for the establishment.
Some fear violence, embracing this alternative, believing that someone will back them up as long as they do not raise steel, relieved smiles on their faces.
Others are worried. They wish to be accepted, fearing rejection by an organization that represents passion and progress. They have raised their palms above their ears, docile and obedient...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: ...Get away from Sonya!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: The outcome is clear, Sonya. The vast majority agree with the proposal.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I hope the Self-Government Group will join in this action. The Assembly needs everyone.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: The votes in favor don't change the fact that this is an ill-considered... ill-advised proposal.

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: You think you're smarter than us, Anna? We know the SSG has been paying lip service to the Assembly, we simply chose not to say it out loud!

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: The SSG needs to prove its loyalty to the Assembly. Enough of your arrogance, Chernobogian.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You want a fight, I'll give you one!

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Leto! No!

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: The Self-Government Group has been utterly committed to finding the best way for all students.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Our doctrine is flexibility, as we have explained to you many times. It is most unfair to criticize the SSG's position now.

steps.name: Faddey
steps.text: Natalya of House Rostov, you may not be a soldier, but you are Ursine nobility, and you should know that obedience is the foundation of our nation's battlefield dominance.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I'll go.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Sonya...?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I'm glad you accept the Assembly's ideals, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I'll go, and I'll join your action, Olga, on one condition.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Any student who refuses to participate is free to pull out without compromising their future status in the Assembly.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Phew... glad that's over.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Dealing with those noble kids is such a headache... brr, Grypherburg nights are awfully cold.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: I'll block the wind for you, Leto!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Thanks, Gummy!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Aha! Got it! C'mere, honey drop!

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Hey! That wasn't nice!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: YOU were the one who lied to me about running out of honey drops!

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Sonya...?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Sorry I made that call for you all, without asking.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: That's not what I meant...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Why apologize, Sonya? You didn't decide anything for us. We chose to join you.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Besides, falling out with the Assembly back there would only make things more difficult for our subsequent operations.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: You're always trying to do the right thing. We trust you.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Natalya is right... but did you agree to Olga's proposal to get the SSG out of a tight spot, or do you genuinely support her action?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: They're rushing into this without planning anything. I'm worried it's gonna get out of hand.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: We're Rhodes Island-trained. If anything unexpected happens, we can help.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I support you too, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I'm just thinking...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why did we come back to Ursus?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Because Rhodes Island doesn't have an office in Ursus, and they need the Self-Government Group to establish an information network here.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: But we could've helped Rhodes Island in other ways. It's not like we've done anything but a little support work since we got to Grypherburg.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We talked about this before we left Rhodes Island. We agreed that the SSG should fight for an office in Ursus.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The Doctor was a little iffy on it, but eventually said yes...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I guess the Doctor wants us to go back to a normal life.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: But... this isn't the normal life I imagined...

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Everyone's fighting all the time. I don't get hungry, but I'm never happy.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: That much is true. Everyone we've met is the same. They keep blather on with big words and concepts, without actually understanding anything.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Is it because we don't know Grypherburg well enough, or because of our unwillingness to reach out to others?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Maybe we've just been away from Ursus for too long. We need time...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: We never truly left Chernobog, did we?
Their faces reflect faintly in the shop windows by the roadside under the dim street lamps. Winter nights in Deity Grypherburg are long and quiet.
They walk old stone-paved streets, trampling chunks of snow into the dirt-filled gaps.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We should have gone back to say goodbye to that old, lifeless place.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: If we keep running from it, the Ursus we remember is just gonna stay charred dirt under broken rubble... And I can't call that home.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: It is the empire's past. It will be the empire's future, if we do nothing.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: The Self-Government Group has seen the fire, while the rest of Ursus has not. We should find the best way forward, however slim the chance may be.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We need friends to get ourselves set up in Grypherburg. That's why we joined the Assembly in the first place.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: I wanna help our new friends!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hah. Besides, the SSG never backs down.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Damn straight!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Are you alright, Zoya?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: ...Young Zoya? Young Zoya!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Are you listening?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I'm sorry, Your Honor.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I find myself fighting my emotions as I relive the events of the general meeting. It was a difficult time for me.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Entirely understandable.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: I'm sure that all present know the background of the Katorga Incident, but I would like you to describe again the circumstances surrounding the Winter Ball at the start of the incident.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Yes, Your Honor.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I spoke to attendees at the ball, and some students who participated in the action shortly after the end of the ball.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I learned that certain unexpected events took place on the day of the ball—
